content.text: {"quote_faithful":"yes","verdict":"confirmed","evidence_kind":"invalid_inference","fatal":"yes","explanation":"The König argument does not prove the pruned tree finite. On an infinite branch, pigeonhole gives a fixed c∈C lying in infinitely many selected sets F_k, but c need not belong to that branch. The instruction “insert c” changes the branch; subsequent selected sets and pruning decisions may therefore differ, so no node of the original branch is shown to be contractible. Thus the claimed contradiction does not follow. The blocker statement is actually true (it admits a short induction on the size of a finite transversal C), so the objection’s assertion that it is false is unsupported; nevertheless, the specific proof written here has a fatal gap, and no separate valid proof appears elsewhere."}
